title: bounded-warmth-regulator-and-utilization-echo-reporter
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Introduce a bounded warm-pool regulator to stabilize warm-set growth and a utilization-echo reporter that emits tenant- and pool-level utilization sketches and sampled percentiles. Improves scale stability and reduces sustained overprovisioning for spiky tenants.
description:
Motivation:
Clusters with aggressive warm-pool prewarming were repeatedly overshooting provisioned capacity for bursty tenants. The existing warm-pool controller allowed rapid growth whenever recent tail spikes were observed, which produced oscillation when spikes were short-lived or noisy (observed during cross-tenant promotional traffic). This PR introduces two complementary components: (1) a bounded warmth regulator that enforces growth cadence and headroom constraints on warm pools, and (2) a utilization-echo reporter that produces lightweight per-pool and per-tenant utilization sketches for more robust admission decisions and offline analysis.

What this change does (high level):
- BoundedWarmthRegulator: A controller that constrains warm-pool ramp-up by applying a per-pool cadence (min-warm-growth-interval) and a proportional cap relative to pool target size and current spare headroom. Growth is throttled when historical spike persistence is low; the regulator also exposes backoff signals to the autoscaler to avoid double-scaling.
- DelegatedEphemeralCredit: A small borrowing API allowing tenants to consume ephemeral credits from a warm pool for short bursts without immediately expanding fleet capacity. Credits decay automatically and are reconciled to prevent long-term drift.
- UtilizationEchoReporter: Periodically samples per-tenant and per-pool active concurrency and token throughput and emits HDR sketches + lightweight percentile samplings (p50/p90/p99) to Prometheus and a compact daily rollup to S3 for long-term analysis. The reporter intentionally samples at variable rates to bound instrumentation overhead.
- Feature flags: gated behind runtime flags (feature.warmth_regulator=true by default on canary) and a tenant opt-out list for customers with custom SLAs.
- Safety and rollback: regulator defaults are conservative; we added automatic fail-open behavior if the regulator detects sustained under-utilization.

Why this is different from previous approaches:
- Moves away from purely reactive prewarming driven by short-window maxima; instead combines persistence-aware cadence with proportional caps to avoid knee-jerk provisioning.
- Delegated credits let us satisfy short spikes cheaply without altering long-term commitment curves.
- UtilizationEchoReporter supplies richer, denoised signals (HDR sketches) that downstream controllers and offline tools can consume to adjust smoothing parameters.

Commits (summary):
- Add BoundedWarmthRegulator controller and unit tests
- Implement DelegatedEphemeralCredit lifecycle and reconciliation
- Add UtilizationEchoReporter, Prometheus metrics, and S3 daily rollup serializer
- Wire feature flags and tenant opt-out configuration
- Update autoscaler to consume regulator backoff signals
- Add e2e tests exercising short spikes and credit consumption

Files changed (high level):
- services/autoscaler/controllers/warmth_regulator.go
- services/autoscaler/controllers/warmth_regulator_test.go
- services/autoscaler/credit/delegated_credit.go
- services/autoscaler/credit/reconcile_test.go
- telemetry/reporters/utilization_echo.go
- telemetry/prometheus/metrics.yaml (adds new metric families)
- infra/feature_flags/defaults.yaml
- docs/ops/warmth-regulator.md
- e2e/tests/warmth_regulator_spike.sh

Testing:
- Unit tests added for regulator cadence logic, credit lifecycle, and reporter sampling (coverage ~86% for modified packages).
- Local e2e script simulates 1,000 tenants with randomized spike durations; tested across 3 warm-pool size profiles.
- Canary rollout on staging cluster ran for 48h with regulated on 20% of pools; CI ran full integration and linting. Initial CI run had a flaky metrics exporter test which was stabilized by retry logic.

Observability and metrics exposed:
- warm_pool_regulator.growth_decisions{pool=\"p1\",decision=\"throttle|allow|failopen\"} counter
- warm_pool_regulator.backoff_seconds gauge (seconds regulator advises autoscaler to wait)
- delegated_credit.consumed_total{tenant=\"t123\"} counter
- delegated_credit.active_credits gauge
- utilization_echo.hdr_sketch{pool=\"p1\",tenant=\"t123\"} (base64-encoded compact sketch in logs for offline aggregator)
- utilization_echo.sampled_percentiles{quantile=\"0.5|0.9|0.99\"} gauge
Notes: HDR sketches are emitted to the long-term S3 rollup only; Prometheus receives sampled percentiles to keep cardinality low.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind flags.
2) Enable on internal staging pools for 48h, observe warm_pool_regulator.growth_decisions and delegated_credit.consumed_total.
3) Enable on 10% of production pools for 24h with automated rollback if pooled headroom drops below safety threshold for 10m.
4) Gradually increase to 50% and then full rollout.

Backward compatibility / migration notes:
- Existing autoscaler behaviour unchanged unless feature flag enabled.
- DelegatedEphemeralCredit persists short-lived entries to existing credit ledger (compatible schema migration with add-only columns).

Related work:
- Refs: ENG-4123 (warm-pool stabilization spike), ENG-4199 (credit accounting improvements), and SUP-8842 (support ticket describing repeated overprovisioning during marketing promos).

Questions for reviewers / open items:
- Are HDR sketch emission intervals acceptable given S3 cost constraints? We set daily rollups by default and allow per-organization overrides.
- DelegatedEphemeralCredit uses a conservative decay constant; ops may want a knob exposed in Console.

Merge outcome:
- Squash-merged after minor test flake fix and two approvals. Canary signals confirmed a 27% reduction in sustained warmset growth and a 9% improvement in average hourly utilization for canaried pools.

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Left a couple of nits in warmth_regulator.go; please add a comment explaining the choice of 30s sampling window. Also request a small defensive check if pool.TargetSize==0.
Ava Chen: Addressed nits, added comment and defensive guard. Updated unit test to include zero-target pool case.

Sofia Patel: Can we limit HDR sketch cardinality? Suggest emitting per-pool only and skipping tenants below 0.1% traffic — otherwise Prometheus will explode.
Ava Chen: Reporter now skips micro-tenants (configurable threshold) and only exposes percentiles to Prometheus; sketches go to S3 as rollups.

Ethan Brooks: Approve after CI fixes. Verified canary metrics and rollback triggers. Would like an ops runbook entry for emergency disable.
